lesson.title: Objects
lesson.summary: Understand objects from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Orientation: why design matters
stage.subtitle: Book chapters 1–2
stage.description: Why projects fail, the accidental success of PHP objects, and how the book is organised.

payload.markdown: I begin Part 1 with a quick look at the history of PHP and objects, charting their shift from afterthought in PHP 3 to core feature in PHP 5.

blocks.text: I begin Part 1 with a quick look at the history of PHP and objects, charting their shift from afterthought in PHP 3 to core feature in PHP 5.

payload.markdown: You can still be an experienced and successful PHP programmer with little or no knowledge of objects. For this reason, I start from first principles to explain objects, classes, and inheritance. Even at this early stage, I look at some of the object enhancements that PHP 5, PHP 7, and PHP 8 introduced.

payload.markdown: The basics established, I delve deeper into our topic, examining PHP’s more advanced object-oriented features. I also devote a chapter to the tools that PHP provides to help you work with objects and classes.

blocks.text: The basics established, I delve deeper into our topic, examining PHP’s more advanced object-oriented features. I also devote a chapter to the tools that PHP provides to help you work with objects and classes.

payload.markdown: It is not enough, however, to know how to declare a class, and to use it to instantiate an object. You must first choose the right participants for your system and decide the best ways for them to interact. These choices are much harder to describe and to learn than the bald facts about object tools and syntax. I finish Part 1 with an introduction to object-oriented design with PHP.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Inheritance: Deriving a class from a base class to reuse and specialise its behaviour.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
CLI Tools: Running PHP from the terminal: plain scripts, Composer scripts and REPL tools.
